short: Public boundary: the AT Protocol adapter (OAuth, PDS, did:plc)
is: The public data boundary: the only crate that knows the AT Protocol — OAuth sign-in, PDS record/blob writes, public profile reads, and real did:plc minting with key custody — quarantining jacquard behind domain port traits.
conventions: Nothing protocol-shaped leaks past this crate's surface (the jacquard client type is a private alias).
Uses `PgPool` as a plain DB client injected by `composition`; its queries run against adapter-pg's migrations.
OAuth at-rest secrets (DPoP key, tokens, PKCE verifier) are envelope-encrypted under the same custody root key as adapter-pg's `key_vault`.
`auth_store` is one of the five documented Unit-of-Work exemptions.
Genesis signatures are atproto-canonical ECDSA-SHA256 low-S via atrium-crypto — never hand-rolled.

Every fetch to a host a visitor, a handle or a DID document names goes through `guarded_http::GuardedHttp`; only `guarded_http/client.rs`, `plc_directory.rs` and `public_records.rs` (operator-configured hosts) may name reqwest, only this crate's manifest may list it (never renamed), and `tests/network_door.rs` fails the build otherwise — it also forbids jacquard's bare-reqwest sessions and resolvers, the named transport-weakening calls (TLS, proxy, address pinning, any redirect policy but `Policy::none()`), and any caller of `AtprotoPublicRecords` outside its own file and the façade, until its transport is settled with the hosted-repos design decision (endpoint from operator config only).

fs.role: 10 statements for OAuth persistence: auth request info (plain and bound to a browser-token hash, that hash read back within the sign-in lifetime, and claimed by clearing it) + session save/get/delete, and delete-every-session-under-an-id (the failed sign-in cleanup)

refs.title: Libraries as Composition — the Approved Crate Set and the Newtype Derive Rules
refs.governs: dev-deps proptest (PLC signing determinism), wiremock (directory/PDS/guarded-client mocks) and tokio-rustls (an untrusted-certificate TLS server for the guarded client); hickory-resolver 0.26 as the guarded client's DNS client (supplies DNS, dictates nothing); jacquard with default features off (no hickory 0.24)

notes: Port → impl: `Authenticator` = `AtprotoAuthenticator` (authenticator.rs) · `IdentityResolver` = `AtprotoIdentityResolver` (resolver/) · `ProfileSource` = `AtprotoProfileSource` · `DidMinter` = `RealDidMinter` / `StubDidMinter` · `PublicRecords` = `AtprotoPublicRecords`. `PlcDirectory` is adapter-local, selected by `plc_directory_from_config`.

`secret_vault::SecretVault` deliberately mirrors adapter-pg's `key_vault::RootKey` (same AEAD, blob format and root key `ZURFUR_DID_KEY_ROOT_KEY`) rather than sharing a type — one adapter may not depend on another. Hoisting the envelope into `domain` is the open follow-up. Root-key custody is DEV-ONLY (config/env) pending a KMS; `composition::ensure_custody_hardened` covers this store too at boot.
Op ordering: `mint` writes custody + the genesis op BEFORE submitting; `tombstone` and `update_handle` submit BEFORE recording, so a failed submit never advances the local chain.
`plc.rs` is pinned to the published vector `did:plc:ewvi7nxzyoun6zhxrhs64oiz`; it is the tripwire for the whole DAG-CBOR → sha256 → base32/24 pipeline.
This crate's half of the `codegen_current` staleness gate lives over in adapter-pg's `tests/it/`, not here.

Guarded web client (`src/guarded_http/`): `policy.rs` = `PublicHttpsUrl` (https, port 443, no userinfo, a domain host of 2+ labels outside the local/reserved TLDs; IP literals refused in every spelling); `address.rs` = the address table (`PublicAddress`: IPv4 deny-list, IPv6 allow-list `2000::/3` with mapped/NAT64 unwrapped); `dns.rs` = `FilteringDns` (fully qualified lookups, 5 s outer timeout, any forbidden answer refuses the name) over one hickory `SystemDns`; `client.rs` = `GuardedHttp` (reqwest 0.12 with the filter as its resolver, no redirects, https-only, no proxy, no decompression, 10 s total timeout, 512 KiB cap with crate-private `send_capped`). Errors split into `Refused` / `NotFound` / `Unavailable` (`errors.rs`). Design record: `.understand/20261008-hardened-resolver-design.md`.

Identity resolver (`src/resolver/`): `handle.rs` = handle → DID (a handle under a reserved TLD such as `.test` is NotFound before any DNS; DNS TXT `_atproto.<handle>.` first, values not `did=` + a DID ignored, two different DIDs → NotFound, NXDOMAIN/empty/too long for DNS → the HTTPS file, any other DNS failure → Unavailable with no fall-through; then `https://<handle>/.well-known/atproto-did`, first line trimmed); `document.rs` = DID → document (only `did:plc` from `https://plc.directory/<did>` and hostname-level `did:web` from `https://<host>/.well-known/did.json`, anything else NotFound with no request; the body must parse as a full jacquard `DidDocument` whose `id` is the DID — mini-docs refused; the claim is the first syntactically valid `at://` handle, a disallowed-TLD first entry is an unusable claim; the PDS is the `#atproto_pds` + `AtprotoPersonalDataServer` service as a `PublicHttpsUrl`); `fetch.rs` = status classes (2xx body; 408/429/5xx Unavailable; else NotFound) and `FetchError` → `ResolveError`; `client.rs` = the struct, the both-ways rules, the 20 s port-call deadline and the logging (the failure class at info, the cause chain only at debug). One `SystemDns` (hickory) serves the A/AAAA filter and the TXT lookups. Test seam: `AtprotoIdentityResolver::over` with scripted DNS (`guarded_http/scripted.rs` answers TXT too) and `GuardedHttp::upstream`; `resolver/client/tests.rs` runs test-support's port conformance suite.

Sign-in (`src/authenticator.rs`): `start(&AtHandle)` is built from jacquard's public pieces, not `start_auth`: `confirm_handle` (both ways) → the document's PDS as a `PublicHttpsUrl` → `get_resource_server_metadata` → the `authorization_endpoint` must pass the URL policy, before the PAR → `par` with `login_hint` = the handle → `account_did` set to the resolved DID → saved. `complete` runs in its own spawned task, so a dropped request cannot cut its cleanup short. After the browser check and the claim (next note) it reads the bound DID from the store (jacquard deletes the request inside `callback`; a request with no bound DID is deleted and refused), runs jacquard's `callback` under a 30 s deadline, and then, outside that deadline: any failure of the attempt that claimed the sign-in, its deadline included, deletes every session stored under `session_id = state` within 5 s (jacquard keys the session it saves by the state, and only the claimer runs the callback, so every such row is its own; `delete_sessions_by_id`, indexed by `client_session_by_session_id`); an attempt that never claimed deletes nothing; on a different `sub` deletes that row first, then revokes best effort via `logout()` within 10 s, and returns the domain's `AccountMismatch`. `start` has a 30 s deadline. Failures are logged at `info` by class only (the resolver's class included); causes only at `debug`; pinned with `resolver/log_recorder.rs`. `authenticator/jacquard_bridge.rs` = `JacquardBridge`, jacquard's only resolver: HTTP through `GuardedHttp`, `resolve_did_doc` = the resolver's checked fetch handed over as the exact validated bytes (20 s deadline: the callback's issuer check), `resolve_handle` always fails (a tripwire), options with every fallback off. Residuals: jacquard saves the session before the account check (the row is deleted afterwards, as above), and its issuer check picks the PDS by type alone (a disagreement fails closed). Test seam: `AtprotoIdentityResolver::scripted` + `GuardedHttp::upstream` + a Postgres auth store.

Browser binding (`src/authenticator.rs`): `start` also mints a 256-bit random token (OsRng, base64url) and saves its SHA-256, never the token, with the auth request in one statement (`save_bound_auth_request`, column `atproto_oauth.auth_request.browser_binding`); it returns the token and the sign-in's lifetime (10 min) for the route's cookie. `complete` checks the presented token first, before reading the bound DID and before any code exchange: no token, no live bound request younger than the lifetime, or a hash that differs (constant-time compare) refuses the callback and deletes the request. A match then claims the sign-in by consuming the binding in one conditional `UPDATE` (`claim_browser_binding`): of callbacks racing on one token, exactly one clears it. Every later callback, a racing loser or a replay, finds the binding cleared (`StoredBinding::Claimed`) and is refused (`Claimed`) without deleting anything, so the request stays the claimer's until jacquard's callback deletes it. A refusal finds no session of its own, so it deletes nothing else.

Profile read (`profile.rs`): one `resolve_did_with_document` call gives the checked DID document and the confirmed handle in a single fetch (an unconfirmed claim shows the DID); the PDS comes from that document (`ResolvedDocument::pds`, URL policy applied) and `getRecord` goes over the resolver's `GuardedHttp` with jacquard's `XrpcExt`; the avatar URL is built on that PDS. The whole read runs under the resolver's port-call deadline (20 s). Any failure but a missing record is an `Err`, so `me` never caches a stripped profile, and it is logged at `info` by a fixed class only.

Test seam, `#[cfg(test)]` only (never a feature): `GuardedHttp::relaxed` (loopback, http, any port), `GuardedHttp::scripted` (strict policy over `guarded_http/scripted.rs`'s scripted DNS), `GuardedHttp::upstream` (strict policy and DNS filter, then plaintext to a mock with `Host` kept). On top of those, `AtprotoIdentityResolver::scripted(http, txt)` builds the resolver over a scripted DNS (the sign-in and profile tests' seam), `with_port_call_deadline` shortens its deadline, and `resolver/log_recorder.rs` is the one global log recorder every test in the crate shares.
